# Model and data

The detector and tracker, and the three datasets, with their licences.

## Model: detector and tracker

### What it is

- **Detector:** YOLO26n (Ultralytics 8.4.182), fine-tuned from Common Objects in Context (COCO) weights on the VisDrone2019 detection training set at an input size of 960 pixels, for 50 epochs on one Tesla T4 graphics processing unit (GPU) (2.7 hours, library defaults otherwise). The best epoch was the last (50), so the model had not finished improving.
- **Tracker:** BoT-SORT from the same library, motion and overlap only (no appearance re-identification, by design), with camera-motion compensation and two confidence thresholds tuned on the validation set (D-321).
- **Exported form:** Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX); its detections match the original exactly on the validation frames checked (D-604).

### Intended use

Research evaluation of detection, tracking and ground-plane distance estimation from low-altitude drone video of road scenes. Not intended for identifying individuals, for safety-critical decisions, or for use outside the tested conditions (see limitations).

### Classes

Trained on VisDrone's ten classes; evaluated as two groups: **person** (pedestrian, people) and **vehicle** (car, van, truck, bus).

### Performance

| Data | Measure | Person | Vehicle |
|---|---|---|---|
| VisDrone detection validation set (all ten classes) | mAP50 / mAP50-95 | 0.415 / 0.240 | (all classes) |
| VisDrone MOT validation frames | AP50 | 0.511 | 0.625 |
| VisDrone MOT test-dev (run once) | AP50 | 0.418 | 0.778 |
| VisDrone MOT test-dev (run once) | Tracking IDF1 / MOTA | 0.436 / 0.264 | 0.760 / 0.635 |
| AU-AIR held-out flights (cross-dataset) | AP50 at IoU 0.5 | 0.025 | 0.209 |

AP50: average precision at an intersection over union (IoU) of 0.5. mAP50-95: mean over IoU 0.5 to 0.95. IDF1: identity F1 score. MOTA: multiple object tracking accuracy.

### Known weaknesses

- Small objects: people 16 to 32 pixels tall are tracked 16% of the time on test-dev.
- Night scenes, partial occlusion and dense queues of similar vehicles cause most misses and identity switches (failure gallery, `results/failures/`).
- On AU-AIR (different camera, many straight-down views) detection transfers poorly at the protocol threshold; AU-AIR's looser boxes explain part of the gap (D-512).

### Training data and licence

VisDrone2019 detection train (with 78 images removed that share source videos with the validation and test-dev tracking clips, D-308). VisDrone states no licence; the weights are not distributed. The code is AGPL-3.0-only, matching Ultralytics.

## Data

*No data is redistributed in this repository. File counts and schema checks come from `results/data_check.json`. Per-file checksums are not recorded: `scripts/data_manifest.py` computes them, but reading the full datasets takes hours and it was not run.*

### VisDrone2019 (tracking and detection)

- **Source:** https://github.com/VisDrone/VisDrone-Dataset. Collected by the AISKYEYE team, Lab of Machine Learning and Data Mining, Tianjin University.
- **Citation:** Zhu, P., Wen, L., Du, D., Bian, X., Fan, H., Hu, Q. and Ling, H. (2021) 'Detection and tracking meet drones challenge', *IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence*, 44(11), pp. 7380-7399. To verify against the journal before publication.
- **Licence and terms (checked 2026-10-19):** no licence file and no stated terms. Used for research evaluation only; not redistributed; only code, metrics and figures are published. Thumbnails in the failure gallery and frames in the demo video are kept minimal and credited.
- **Used:** tracking (MOT) train, validation and test-dev; detection (DET) train and validation.
- **Splits:** DET train for training; DET validation for model selection; MOT validation for tracker tuning; MOT test-dev once, at the end.
- **Known issue (D-308):** VisDrone's statement that its image set does not overlap its videos is false; 78 overlapping detection images were removed from training and selection.

### Mid-Air (distance ground truth, synthetic)

- **Source:** https://midair.ulg.ac.be; scripts at https://github.com/montefiore-ai/midair-dataset.
- **Citation:** Fonder, M. and Van Droogenbroeck, M. (2019) 'Mid-Air: a multi-modal dataset for extremely low altitude drone flights', *Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops*. To verify before publication.
- **Licence:** Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Not redistributed.
- **Used:** one climate (Kite_training, sunny), 30 flights: depth, segmentation, surface normals and colour images of the left camera, plus flight records.
- **Splits:** by flight, seed 0: 15 development, 6 calibration, 9 test (`results/splits.json`).
- **Limitation:** synthetic, with no people or vehicles; it validates the geometry, not the detector.

### AU-AIR (real drone footage)

- **Source:** https://bozcani.github.io/auairdataset (authors' page); also indexed at https://fmi-data-index.github.io/au_air.html.
- **Citation:** Bozcan, I. and Kayacan, E. (2020) 'AU-AIR: a multi-modal unmanned aerial vehicle dataset for low altitude traffic surveillance', *IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)*. To verify before publication.
- **Licence:** the third-party index states CC BY 4.0; The authors' annotation file lists CC BY-NC-SA 2.0 and CC BY-NC 2.0. The stricter reading is used: non-commercial research, attributed, and no AU-AIR images in this repository (D-323).
- **Used:** all 32,823 annotated frames (5 frames per second, 8 recordings, 48 clips), with per-frame GPS position, altitude and drone attitude.
- **Splits:** calibration recordings 20190829091111 and 20190905142119 for the camera model; the other six held out (D-506).
- **Findings about the data:** altitude is in millimetres and drifts by metres within a flight; the camera tilt is not recorded; annotation boxes are looser than tight boxes (D-512) and not consistent from frame to frame (D-516); the paper's stated camera angles (45-90°) do not cover all clips (D-504).

### SynDrone (end-to-end truth, synthetic; version 2)

- **Source:** https://github.com/LTTM/Syndrone (generation code, Apache-2.0); data at https://lttm.dei.unipd.it/paper_data/syndrone/.
- **Citation:** Rizzoli, G., Barbato, F., Caligiuri, M. and Zanuttigh, P. (2023) 'SynDrone: multi-modal UAV dataset for urban scenarios', *IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)*; arXiv:2308.10491. To verify before publication.
- **Licence (checked 2026-11-04):** neither the download page nor the paper states one. The authors' own arXiv comment reads "downloadable dataset with CC-BY license", with no version. Treated as Creative Commons Attribution (attribution required); no SynDrone images are committed to this repository, and contact sheets stay in `cache/`.
- **Used:** CARLA-rendered flights over eight towns, 120 s each at 25 frames per second, each seen by three cameras (20 m at 30° below the horizon, 50 m at 60°, 80 m straight down): colour, depth, semantic labels, camera poses and 3D boxes with persistent actor identities. Read member by member from the archives with HTTP range requests (D-702).
- **Splits:** by town, stratified by town type, seed 0: development Town01, Town07, Town10HD; calibration Town04, Town05; test Town02, Town03, Town06 (`results/splits.json`, D-701). The official split is by frame within each town and is not used.
- **Limitation:** synthetic imagery from an ideal pinhole camera, with CARLA's traffic and pedestrian behaviour.

### HIT-UAV (thermal detection; version 2, Phase 13)

- **Source:** https://github.com/suojiashun/HIT-UAV-Infrared-Thermal-Dataset, commit 669259659b21a2737ca9f5e4bc81892acbe6ecd8 (`configs/thermal.yaml`).
- **Citation:** Suo, J., Wang, T., Zhang, X., Chen, H., Zhou, W. and Shi, W. (2023) 'HIT-UAV: a high-altitude infrared thermal dataset for unmanned aerial vehicle-based object detection', *Scientific Data*, 10, 227. doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02066-6.
- **Licence (checked 2026-11-10):** CC BY 4.0, from the repository's LICENSE file (D-748). Use, change and redistribution allowed, including commercial, with credit. No HIT-UAV images are committed here.
- **Used:** 2,898 thermal images, 640 x 512, DJI Zenmuse XT2 on a DJI Matrice M210 V2, 60 to 130 m, camera 30 to 90 degrees down, by day and night. Person, Car and Bicycle map to the detector's VisDrone classes; OtherVehicle and DontCare are ignored regions.
- **Splits:** by capture day (D-751): validation 23 January 2021, test 16 and 21 January 2021, training the other six days, because the official random split puts frames of the same videos in training and test. The official split is used once, for comparison with published results (`results/hituav/splits.json`).

### BIRDSAI (thermal tracking; version 2, Phase 13)

- **Source:** LILA, "Conservation Drones" (https://lila.science/datasets/conservationdrones), real training and test archives (SHA-256 in `Data/birdsai/zips/sha256.txt`); the simulated set is not used.
- **Citation:** Bondi, E., Jain, R., Aggrawal, P., Anand, S., Hannaford, R., Kapoor, A., Piavis, J., Shah, S., Joppa, L., Dilkina, B. and Tambe, M. (2020) 'BIRDSAI: a dataset for detection and tracking in aerial thermal infrared videos', *IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)*.
- **Licence (checked 2026-11-10):** Community Data License Agreement, permissive variant, as stated on the LILA page (D-754). No BIRDSAI images are committed here.
- **Used:** 48 real night-time thermal videos from fixed-wing drone patrols over African protected areas (FLIR Vue Pro 640 or Tamarisk 640, 640 x 480, 60 to 120 m), humans and animals tracked frame by frame. People only are scored; animals count as false alarms, not ignored.
- **Splits:** the dataset's own: 32 training videos (6 with people) tune the tracker; 16 test videos (5 with people) are scored once.

## Code from other projects (version 2)

- **TrackEval** (https://github.com/JonathonLuiten/TrackEval, commit 12c8791, MIT licence, checked from its LICENSE file 2026-11-04): the Higher Order Tracking Accuracy (HOTA) computation is vendored in `src/aerialrange/track/hota.py` with its copyright notice, changed only to run on NumPy 2.

## Tracker (version 2)

The project's own tracker (`src/aerialrange/track/tracker.py`, D-713) replaces the detector library's BoT-SORT. It is written from the published methods (ByteTrack: Zhang et al., 2022; BoT-SORT: Aharon et al., 2022; DeepSORT noise weights: Wojke et al., 2017) and contains no code from them. It uses motion and box overlap only; no appearance features are computed.

## Package dependencies (version 2, licences checked 2026-11-07)

The package (`src/aerialrange`) no longer uses Ultralytics (D-725). Its pinned environment, `requirements-lock.txt`, was built from `pyproject.toml` alone in a clean Python 3.12 and holds no PyTorch and no GPL or AGPL code. Licences below are read from each installed package's own metadata (its licence expression, or its licence classifiers where it has none).

| Package | Licence |
|---|---|
| numpy | BSD-3-Clause (bundled parts: 0BSD, MIT, Zlib, CC0-1.0) |
| scipy, pandas | BSD |
| opencv-python-headless | Apache-2.0 |
| onnxruntime | MIT |
| onnx | Apache-2.0 |
| onnxslim | MIT |
| pillow | MIT-CMU |
| matplotlib | Matplotlib licence (PSF-based) |
| h5py, psutil | BSD-3-Clause |
| pyyaml, typer, motmetrics | MIT |
| Indirect: contourpy, cycler, kiwisolver, colorama, mpmath, sympy, protobuf, pygments, python-dateutil | BSD (python-dateutil also Apache-2.0) |
| Indirect: fonttools, pyparsing, rich, markdown-it-py, mdurl, six, annotated-doc, xmltodict, shellingham | MIT (shellingham ISC) |
| Indirect: flatbuffers, ml_dtypes, packaging, tzdata, typing_extensions | Apache-2.0 (packaging also BSD-2-Clause; typing_extensions PSF-2.0) |
| Development only: pytest, pytest-cov, pluggy, iniconfig, ruff, coverage | MIT (coverage Apache-2.0) |
| Development only: pymap3d 3.1.0 (test reference for the geodetic conversion, Phase 12; licence read from its LICENSE file 2026-11-09: two conditions, BSD-2-Clause) | BSD-2-Clause |

Version 1's results can still be reproduced in a separate environment, `requirements-v1.txt`, which adds PyTorch and Ultralytics 8.4.182 (AGPL-3.0); the scripts that need it load the library through `scripts/ultralytics_v1.py`. The version 1 detector's weights were trained with that library from its COCO weights, which Ultralytics distributes under AGPL-3.0; running them through the project's own ONNX runner removes the library, not the weights' terms.

## Detector candidates (version 2, licences checked 2026-11-06)

The version 1 detector and its library are AGPL-3.0, so version 2 replaces them. Each candidate's licence was read from the LICENSE file in its own repository; the weights' terms from the repository's own statements and the place the weights are hosted. Only the sizes listed are candidates.

| Candidate | Code licence | Pretrained weights | Pretraining data |
|---|---|---|---|
| RF-DETR Nano, Small, Medium (https://github.com/roboflow/rf-detr) | Apache-2.0 | Apache-2.0, stated for these sizes in the README; backbone DINOv2, Apache-2.0 | COCO; the paper's training recipe includes Objects365 pretraining |
| D-FINE N, S, M (https://github.com/Peterande/D-FINE) | Apache-2.0 | Hosted in the authors' weights repository, licensed Apache-2.0 | COCO only, or Objects365 then COCO (both published) |
| DEIM, D-FINE and RT-DETRv2 variants (https://github.com/Intellindust-AI-Lab/DEIM) | Apache-2.0 | Hosted on Google Drive with no separate terms; the repository licence covers the project | COCO only for the sizes considered |
| RT-DETRv2 R18, R34 (https://github.com/lyuwenyu/RT-DETR) | Apache-2.0 | Hosted in the author's weights repository, which has no licence file | COCO only, or Objects365 then COCO |
| YOLOX Nano, Tiny, S (https://github.com/Megvii-BaseDetection/YOLOX) | Apache-2.0 | Release assets of the Apache-2.0 repository | COCO |
| NanoDet-Plus (https://github.com/RangiLyu/nanodet) | Apache-2.0 | Release assets of the Apache-2.0 repository (no commits since 2024) | COCO |

**Excluded:** DEIMv2 (its 2026 licence allows non-commercial use only); RF-DETR Atto, Femto, Pico, XLarge and 2XLarge (Roboflow Platform Model License 1.0: commercial self-hosting needs a paid add-on); the original YOLOv7 and YOLOv9 repositories (GPL-3.0).

**Open question, pretraining data:** Objects365's own site states no licence; a third-party listing describes it as non-commercial. Weights pretrained on it may inherit that restriction, so the COCO-only weights are preferred where a candidate offers both, and the choice is recorded with the result. COCO's annotations are CC-BY 4.0 and its images carry their Flickr licences; ImageNet-pretrained backbones carry ImageNet's research terms. These questions apply to almost every published detector, the version 1 one included. Not legal advice.

## Phase 11 reference tools (licences checked 2026-11-09)

Neither is a dependency of `src/aerialrange` (build2 R13); both live under `tools/openvins/` and are used only to produce a reference trajectory for comparison.

| Tool | Licence | Use |
|---|---|---|
| OpenVINS v2.7 (https://github.com/rpng/open_vins) | GPL-3.0 (LICENSE file in the repository) | Built and run in its own container (`tools/openvins/Dockerfile`) on converted Mid-Air flights; only its output trajectories are compared. Its code never enters `src/`. |
| rosbags 0.11.9 (https://gitlab.com/ternaris/rosbags) | Apache-2.0 (package metadata, `License-Expression`) | Writes the ROS 1 bags OpenVINS reads (`tools/openvins/make_bag.py`), installed in a separate folder (`cache/venvs/rosbags_lib`). |

The navigation filter itself (`src/aerialrange/navigation/`) uses only NumPy, SciPy and OpenCV, already listed above. Its method is from the published papers cited in `docs/navigation.md`; no OpenVINS code was copied, and only OpenVINS's published configuration values are used as settings.
